summary: The third fsync run was accepted, so the heartbeat account now holds three executions of its persisted-term surface in one band and its limitation reports all three with the unchanged platform caveat. The thinnest remaining measurement is the VerifyLeader lease contrast, which has run once: it recorded a 500 ms lease failing at 510 ms and a 1 s lease failing at 1018 ms, the bound on how long a false self-verification survives before the lease check removes the leader. I requested a repeat of 64b6f78684b04f8ea393a5827f5457c7-experiment from its retained inputs, which reruns both lease cases with no code change. A similar pair keeps the account's explanation, its six counterevidence items and five limitations exactly as recorded while turning the bound into a two-run observation; a materially different pair would reopen how the account states the exposure that a successful verification buys, which is the part of that question a reader is most likely to rely on. The request validates against the schema and makes no other edits.
